remediation.issue: The relative documentation link uses parent directory traversal syntax.
remediation.suggestion: Replace ../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE.md with a package-relative or repository-root reference when publishing.

content.value_statement: Large codebases make architecture and data relationships hard to trace. This skill maps Empathy Ledger files, services, routes, and database domains for guided exploration.
actual_capabilities: Identifies key database type files by domain.
Maps Supabase client usage across browser, server, and service-role contexts.
Lists core service layer files and their business purpose.
Shows main API route groups for stories, projects, embeds, and administration.
Explains the expected data flow from React components to PostgreSQL.
Provides read-only exploration commands for locating files and references.
limitations: It is tailored to the Empathy Ledger repository structure.
It does not inspect runtime behavior without repository access.
It does not replace security review of service-role or admin code.
It may become outdated if files or routes are reorganized.

use_cases.title: Find a feature owner
use_cases.description: Locate the service, API route, type file, and component area connected to a product feature.

use_cases.title: Trace tenant data flow
use_cases.description: Understand how tenant filtering should move through API routes, services, Supabase clients, and database tables.

use_cases.title: Prepare architecture notes
use_cases.description: Create concise maps of database domains, services, and route groups before planning changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find a file area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use codebase-explorer to find where the Empathy Ledger codebase handles [feature or table]. Include likely files and route groups.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use codebase-explorer to explain how [workflow] moves from React components through API routes, services, Supabase, and database tables.

prompt_templates.title: Map related domains
prompt_templates.prompt: Use codebase-explorer to map the files, services, tables, and relationships involved in [domain]. Note the safest entry points to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Audit tenant boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use codebase-explorer to trace tenant isolation for [feature]. Identify expected filters, service boundaries, and files that need careful review.

output_examples.output: The answer identifies the story ownership type file, distribution service, story distribution API route group, consent proof tables, and revocation touchpoints.

output_examples.input: How does tenant isolation work for projects?
output_examples.output: The response explains that project access should connect profile tenant data, route checks, service logic, and tenant-scoped database queries.

output_examples.input: What should I inspect before changing embedded stories?
output_examples.output: The response highlights embed routes, embed service logic, story distribution records, consent proof handling, and related media or transcript tables.

best_practices: Ask for one feature or domain at a time to keep the map focused.
Verify listed files against the current repository before editing.
Review service-role and admin paths with extra care because they can bypass normal row policies.
anti_patterns: Do not assume the reference map is complete after major repository reorganizations.
Do not run exploration commands outside the intended repository.
Do not treat architecture guidance as proof that access controls are implemented correctly.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users understand where Empathy Ledger features, data types, services, routes, and database relationships are located.

faq.question: Can it modify the codebase?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides navigation guidance and read-only exploration patterns, not code changes.

faq.question: Does it work outside Empathy Ledger?
faq.answer: It is written for the Empathy Ledger repository and may not match other project structures.

faq.question: Does it explain Supabase usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It names the browser, server, and service-role client areas and explains their intended contexts.

faq.question: Does it cover tenant isolation?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes the expected tenant filtering pattern and where to inspect it.

faq.question: Should I still review the actual files?
faq.answer: Yes. Use this skill as a map, then verify behavior in the current source files.
